channels.intro: Status, permissions and switches for each account in the Care core. Zalo and Email log in in their source module; Telegram logs in right here (QR code or login code; connection keys are never entered in the UI).

cutoverAction.complete_core: Complete: move to the Care core

cutoverBody.prepare: The account will drain: the module holding send ownership stops accepting new work while the system checks the conditions. Ownership doesn't change until you complete it.
cutoverBody.complete_core: Moves write and send ownership to the Care core. The legacy module will no longer send for this account.
cutoverBody.complete_legacy: Returns write and send ownership to the legacy module. The Care core will no longer send for this account.
cutoverBody.abort: Stops the cutover and keeps the current owner.

rules.title: Care agent rules
rules.intro: Rules decide which agent handles which conversation and in what mode. A narrower scope always beats a broader one; within the same scope the higher priority wins; two equal rules conflict and are rejected.
rules.emptyHint: With no rules, the agent handles no conversations (result: not applicable).
rules.deleteBody: Conversations under this rule will fall back to a broader rule (or to no rule).

scopeHint.channel: Applies to every account on one channel.
scopeHint.customer: Applies to one customer (optionally limited to an account).

rules.priorityHint: The higher number wins within the same scope. Default is 100.

modeHint.observe: The agent drafts nothing and only records.
modeHint.draft: The agent writes a draft; a person reviews it before it is sent.
modeHint.auto: The agent sends on its own when conditions are met (still honoring quiet hours, quotas, and pausing when a person replies).

rules.telegramAi: The Telegram agent is blocked by design in this version: rules only take effect as observe.
rules.denyWarning: A disabled rule isn't just skipped: it blocks the agent for exactly this scope, and broader rules do NOT take over.

rules.policyHint: Leave empty to use the channel default. Only fields you fill in will override it.

tgbot.title: Telegram Bot
tgbot.intro: Add an official Telegram bot (created with BotFather) to your care groups to read group messages and answer customers. This is separate from the personal-account (MTProto) connection.

limits.title: Bot API limits
limits.onlyAdded: The bot only sees groups it was added to, and has no history from before it joined.
limits.privacy: With privacy mode on, in a group the bot only sees commands, replies to it and messages mentioning it.
limits.deletes: Telegram does not send delete events to bots: deleted messages stay in Care.
limits.dm: A customer who wants a private chat must message the bot first.
limits.edits: Edited messages are delivered and updated.

add.title: Add a bot
add.step1: Open @BotFather in Telegram, send /newbot and follow the prompts.
add.step2: Copy the token BotFather gives you (looks like 123456:ABC…).
add.step3: Paste it below. The token is checked with Telegram and stored encrypted; afterwards only the last 4 characters are shown.
add.step4: Use a SEPARATE bot for Care, not the FreedomOS control bot.

add.TOKEN_REJECTED: Telegram did not accept this token.

privacy.title: Privacy mode is on
privacy.body: In groups the bot only receives commands, replies to it and messages mentioning it. To read every group message:
privacy.botfather: Open @BotFather → /mybots → pick the bot → Bot Settings.
privacy.group_privacy: Go to Group Privacy → Turn off.
privacy.readd: Remove the bot from each group and add it again (Telegram only applies the change when the bot rejoins).
privacy.or_admin: Or make the bot an administrator in the group: an admin bot reads every message.

banner.token_invalid: Telegram rejected the token. Add the bot again with a new token from BotFather; receiving has stopped.
banner.webhook_conflict: The bot has a webhook set, or another program is reading updates with the same token. Only one place can receive them; delete the webhook or stop the other program.
banner.unreachable: Couldn't reach the Telegram Bot API (network or timeout). It will retry on its own.

bridge.title: Bring accounts into the shared inbox
bridge.intro: The shared inbox mirrors the messages of your existing Zalo / Email accounts. Replies sent from here still go through the existing senders, so the anti-ban limits and quiet hours keep applying.
bridge.notReady: The server has no valid Care encryption key (DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be exactly 64 hex characters), so the shared inbox cannot be enabled yet.

bridge.emptyHint: Connect accounts under Channels & agents (scan the Zalo QR, connect Gmail), then turn on “Add to the shared inbox”.

bridge.pausedHint: The copy is unfinished and nothing is running it (cancelled, the app restarted or it failed). Press “Resume copying”: it continues where it stopped.
bridge.driftedHint: The last check found {n} items that differ between the old data and the shared inbox. Press “Catch up now”, then “Verify” again; if it still differs, turn this account off and on again.
bridge.notVerified: No check has been recorded yet.
bridge.ownerCore: The shared inbox owns this account (cutover done)

dialog.title: Bring “{label}” into the shared inbox
dialog.lead: Read this before you turn it on:
dialog.readOnly: Read-only mirror: copies this account's customers, conversations and messages into the shared inbox. It does NOT send, does NOT create sending jobs and does NOT turn on Care's AI or auto-reply.
dialog.sender: The sender does NOT change: the account stays owned by the old system, which keeps sending exactly as today.
dialog.cost: It has a performance cost: from now on every write to this account's legacy data also runs a journalling trigger. Measured on synthetic data (evidence cc-23): writes are about 4.3–9.3× slower than without it, and the journal is large (about 374 MB for 100,000 short writes). Not measured on your real data.
dialog.journal: Applied journal entries are pruned automatically (kept 24 hours); the text of deleted messages is removed from the journal within a minute.
dialog.background: The history is copied in the background in small batches; you can cancel and resume, and progress shows on this screen. A large account can take minutes to tens of minutes.
dialog.off: To turn it off: press “Turn off” next to the account. Copied data is kept; turning it on again copies from scratch. Turn the shared inbox off before going back to an older build.
dialog.reasonHint: For example: trying the shared inbox for shop A
dialog.understood: I have read and understood the above

disableDialog.title: Turn the shared inbox off for “{label}”?
disableDialog.body: Stops journalling and syncing for this account. What was copied stays in the shared inbox but will no longer update. The old Zalo / Email screens open again for this account.

rules.title: Who answers where
rules.precedence: The more specific rule wins: conversation › customer › account › channel. Each conversation can still change its AI mode in the inbox.
rules.emptyHint: Add a rule to choose which agent answers for each account.
rules.pickIntro: Pick a kind of rule. Zalo and Gmail write straight into the assignments the running agents follow.

pick.zalo: Assign an agent to a Zalo nick: all 1-1 chats, all groups or one conversation.
pick.noZalo: Needs a Zalo nick and at least one agent.
pick.email: Assign an agent to a Gmail inbox: all mail, one domain or one sender.
pick.noEmail: Needs a Gmail inbox and at least one agent.
pick.core: Care rule for accounts the Care runtime runs (for example a Telegram bot).
